https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/news/brist.text: This is the moment a killer was caught on CCTV buying a hi-vis workman’s vest to use as a disguise before the brutal kidnapping and murder of a dad-of-two. Four men, including one from Bristol, have now been jailed for murdering Tomasz Samel, who was tortured, doused in petrol and set alight over a missing £1million cigarette haul. The 45-year-old was ambushed and snatched from an address in Handsworth, Birmingham, by gangsters posing as Interpol officers at around 8.40am on March 27, 2019. A court heard he was then driven to the Liverpool area in a white Peugeot van, where he was stripped naked and set on fire "to teach him a lesson". After being dumped by the roadside, he banged on the door of a property in Bickerstaffe, Lancs, at 11.10pm that night, suffering from 75 per cent burns. Tomasz was rushed to hospital and treated in a specialist burns unit in Liverpool, but died three months later on June 21. Neil Jones, 48, of no fixed address, and Tobiasz Kozlowski, 38, Kirkby, Merseyside, were found guilty of murder and jailed for life at Birmingham Crown Court on Friday (9/10). Kevin Wooden, 46, and Kye Arthur, 35, of Bristol, were found guilty of manslaughter and sentenced to 23 years and 22 years, respectively. Kozlowski's wife, Sandra Kozlowska, 38, of Kirkby, was found guilty of assisting an offender after helping her husband while he was on the run. She deposited money into a bank account for him and also began formulating a cover story with him to use if he were arrested. She was sentenced to three years in jail, suspended for three years. The court was told Tomasz, who was originally from Poland, was kidnapped in front of his wife and children by the men who said they were carrying out a European Arrest Warrant. Detectives later uncovered that the brutal attack was linked to a £1million illicit cigarette smuggling operation. Tomasz had been linked to a storage unit in Aston, Birmingham, which was raided by HMRC weeks before the kidnapping, with officers seizing 10 million illegal cigarettes. The massive haul dealt a crippling blow to the criminal enterprise, and prosecutors said he was blamed for the loss. Police found that Kozlowski and Jones led the plot to kidnap and "teach a lesson" to Tomasz. They were key figures in the cigarette smuggling operation and had travelled to Poland to discuss the loss of the 10 million cigarettes and formulate a plan to kidnap Tomasz. Jones later admitted that he paid the kidnappers £20,000 to take Tomasz. Wooden, who was captured on camera buying a high-vis jacket, had purchased a police-style earpiece from Amazon so he could pass off as an Interpol officer along with Arthur. He also acquired the van, which was used to drive Tomasz to his death, and was captured on CCTV at a Starbucks at Hopwood Services on the M42 around an hour before the kidnapping. An emotionless Wooden was also captured on camera being arrested by officers after extradition from the Dominican Republic. Body-cam footage also shows the moment a shocked-looking Jones was arrested after being extradited from Greece, whilst already serving a 30-year sentence for trafficking £42 million worth of cocaine. Chief Supt Scott Griffiths, of West Midlands Police, said after the case: “Tomasz would have suffered an unimaginable amount of pain when he was tortured, and his agony continued for the months leading up to his death. “The violence that was inflicted on him does not bear thinking about, and those that were willing to do that to another human being are clearly very dangerous individuals. “Our investigation has spanned many years and many countries, as we pieced together people’s movements, mobile phone data, CCTV, and other information to build a picture of what happened on that night. “I’m pleased that after more than seven years, we have finally been able to get justice for Tomasz and his family, and hope that it will offer some small level of comfort to those who knew and loved him. “This was a significant organised crime group, making millions of pounds through the illegal trade of cigarettes, with operations across a number of countries. “Our investigation took us to Poland, Greece, the Dominican Republic, Mexico, Colombia, France and Scotland and Wales where these organised criminals had operations or fled to in the aftermath of the kidnap. "I’d like to thank the Crown Prosecution Service for their support as we worked to bring a successful case against these individuals.” Kate Seal, from the Crown Prosecution Service, said: "This was a brutal attack on a man who was kidnapped from his own home and subjected to horrendous violence. "The CPS worked closely with West Midlands Police throughout this lengthy and complex investigation to pursue lines of enquiry and build a case using forensic, digital and witness evidence. “Our thoughts remain with Mr Samel’s family, who have endured unimaginable suffering, including witnessing his abduction from their family home. "I hope these verdicts provide some measure of closure and reassurance that justice has been achieved."
